items.title: SGLang matches DeepSeek's DeepInfer engine on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash for both prefill and decode, with a reproduction guide
items.summary: SGLang reports parity with DeepInfer on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: up to 1.04x prefill throughput on 4x GB300 and 4x B300, and up to 7.4% higher decode throughput on 64x GB300. It ships an end-to-end reproduction guide and a production serving stack, so open serving now keeps pace with DeepSeek's own engine.

items.title: Kimi K3.1 ranks #1 among open-weight models on the Vals Index (#8 overall)
items.summary: Vals AI's aggregate index places Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 first among open-weight models and eighth overall, a second independent ranking after Agent Arena that puts it at the top of open models.

doubt.pushback: Results are shown only as an image, and @scaling01 notes many users find Kimi K3.1 disappointing in practice despite its rankings.

items.title: Anthropic guide: fold routers, planners and domain subagents into one agent loop with skills and tool search
items.summary: Anthropic's Applied AI team (guide dated Oct 22) reports that across several enterprise deployments a single agent loop with skills often beat both one-prompt and subagent designs on quality, cost and latency, with one customer seeing about 2x faster runtime. It gives a migration method: fold one subagent at a time, check with a small end-to-end eval run repeatedly, and keep subagents only for context bloat, disposable parallel work, or tool-choice problems past 30 to 50 tools.

doubt.pushback: The 2x figure is one customer's comparison, not a benchmark; repliers stress that merged agents can regress on specific tasks (Anthropic's own example skipped a required lookup), so evals need repeated runs per task.

reception.summary: Most repliers say they reached the same conclusion building their own agents (fewer handoffs, less lost context, fewer shell commands), with a minority calling it lock-in or noting labs trained models to use subagents.

items.title: LiteLLM adds official OpenCode Go support
items.summary: LiteLLM can now route OpenCode Go subscription models through an existing proxy setup, picking the right upstream API, keeping the conversation session, and logging estimated usage under OpenCode Go.

doubt.pushback: No changelog or docs link in the post.

items.title: CUADebug traces computer-use agent failures to root causes and lifts OSWorld success from 61.2% to 66.5%
items.summary: An EMNLP 2026 paper that diagnoses why a computer-use agent failed and guides its recovery, raising OSWorld success by about 5 points, with a project page and arXiv paper.
